author: WP12
summary: Rewritten for the Bible's pin into a CNB chapter with a closing CNJ section: container contract, schemas, compression and mmap, runtime integration, CNJ's role and tooling. Mostly current; wrong in a few details at TARGET (CRC over stored bytes not logical data, custom ids hashed case-sensitively, no sorting in the writer, the type check after construction). The site's CNB Format page already held the container at byte level; the CNJ relationship, parser split and path rules now live on a new CNJ deep dive.

concepts.text: CNB is CNA's native compiled runtime format: one .cnb file describes one typed asset; it is neither an archive nor an interchange format.
tokens: Not a package or archive
Not an interchange format

concepts.text: PNG, WAV and glTF are source formats, CNJ is editable JSON and CNB is the deterministic shipping representation produced by the pipeline.
tokens: .cnj is how it is edited; .cnb is how it ships

concepts.text: CNB shares neither XNB's reader-name graph nor its compression framing.
tokens: it shares no code with XNB

concepts.text: Container 1.0 starts with a 64-byte little-endian header and a bounded table of contents whose entries record chunk id, offset, stored and logical sizes, flags and a CRC-32C.
tokens: The 64-byte header
Table of contents: 48 bytes per chunk

concepts.text: Chunks may be compressed independently with Zstandard.
tokens: Implemented when CNA is built with libzstd

concepts.text: Claim that the CRC is checked over the logical (decompressed) data: at the snapshot each chunk's CRC-32C covers its stored bytes and is verified before any decompressor sees them.
tokens: The chunk checksum covers the stored bytes
concepts.note: Bible said logical data; TARGET checksums stored bytes.

concepts.text: CRC-32C detects accidental corruption; it is not authentication, and applications accepting untrusted downloads need a separate signature or trusted transport.
tokens: Not tamper-proof

concepts.text: Built-in schemas exist for Texture2D, Texture3D, TextureCube, SpriteFont, Model, AnimationClip, Curve, SoundEffect, Song and Video; Effect's identifier is reserved without a schema.
tokens: Identifier reserved, no schema, by design

concepts.text: Model schema 2 extends the model encoding (exact XNA vertex declarations, shared buffers, stock effects) while schema 1 decoding is preserved; the loader picks the decoder from the header's schema version.
tokens: The loader picks the decoder from the header's schema version

concepts.text: Schema ids, chunk ids and asset-type ids are frozen wire values independent of C++ enum order, and each built-in schema has a producer and a runtime loader.
tokens: The numeric values of the built-in types are frozen

concepts.text: Texture payloads can carry several representations for the runtime to choose from, but schema 1 writes Rgba8 only and the loader uploads only Rgba8, so the selection has one true case today.
tokens: this build can upload none of them
concepts.note: Bible implied renderer-matched representations; TARGET uploads Rgba8 only.

concepts.text: Model data carries vertex and index bytes, meshes, materials, skeleton, animation, morph targets and lights for the shared model builder.
tokens: morph targets and weight keys, skinning skeleton

concepts.text: Song and Video stay streaming assets: the CNB holds metadata and a bounded logical external reference while the pipeline deploys the media bytes beside it.
tokens: Metadata plus a reference, never the media

concepts.text: Claim that custom ids derive from a stable lowercase name: at the snapshot CnbAssetTypeIdFromName hashes the exact UTF-8 bytes (FNV-1a-32 OR 0x80000000), case-sensitively; custom files must carry CMET metadata and a process-wide registry maps the id plus name to a loader.

concepts.text: The CNB extension model is deliberately smaller than XNB's assembly-qualified reader system.
tokens: CNB's extension model is deliberately much smaller than XNB's

concepts.text: Writers finish a complete container in memory and the tools publish atomically; Claim that metadata is sorted for determinism: CnbWriter emits chunks and external references in the order they were added and determinism comes from that fixed order and zero-filled gaps.

atomic rename

concepts.text: Compression is chosen per chunk and a chunk is stored compressed only when that made it smaller.
tokens: A chunk is stored compressed only if that made it smaller

concepts.text: Measurements retained in CNA compare size and decode cost on real assets and conclude compression slows loading on fast NVMe, which is why it is opt-in.
tokens: CNA-reported measurements, not guarantees

concepts.text: The mmap investigation did not justify zero-copy: validation, checksums and object construction still need owned work and hardware CRC made the material difference, so memory mapping is documented as measured and rejected.
tokens: Memory mapping: measured and rejected

concepts.text: ContentManager checks name.xnb, then name.cnb, then loose and CNJ candidates; CNB is self-describing, so it is dispatched before a per-type loose reader and needs no reader on the manager.
tokens: The file is self-describing, so this tier needs no reader registered

concepts.text: The loader validates container and schema, resolves external references through the manager and builds the runtime object; the requested-type check is an any_cast of the built result, so a wrong T is refused after construction.
tokens: raised after the loader has already built the object
The result must be exactly the T you asked for
concepts.note: Bible placed the type check before construction.

concepts.text: CNJ remains ordinary JSON for authoring and compatibility, describing self-contained assets or referring to source files, consumed by runtime loose readers and the build-time pipeline.
tokens: What CNJ is, and what it is not

concepts.text: CNJ has no magic bytes, fixed binary schema or chunk checksum; a shipped CNJ pays parse and conversion costs at run time and has weaker size and depth controls than CNB (none at all at the snapshot).
tokens: no magic bytes, no fixed binary schema and no checksum
What CNJ does not bound

concepts.text: CNB does not embed JSON: the pipeline parses CNJ into the same typed description other importers produce and writes the frozen schema, so that shared description, not byte similarity, is the compatibility boundary.
tokens: CNB does not embed JSON

concepts.text: The runtime readers and the CNJ-to-CNB compilers read documents through the same canonical CnjCanonicalRead functions, so a document means the same thing at run time and build time.
tokens: a document means the same thing at run time and at build time

concepts.text: The tree includes direct glTF-to-CNB and source-to-CNB tools plus cna_tool_cnb_info for inspection and validation.
